messages:
maria: Hey team — started seeing OOMs on the paged-attn runtime after yesterday's fused-attn kernel change. Repro on a dedicated instance with long chat sessions. Pasting the tail of the worker log I have:

maria: ```
E 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z worker-7 OOM while allocating block-table slab (requested 24MB)
E 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z worker-7 kv_pager: total_pages=19648 resident_pages=19648 free_pages=0
E 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z worker-7 pager: attempted to evict but active_slots=1200 pinned_slots=320
W 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z worker-7 fallback: falling back to non-paged KV access for request
E 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z worker-7 runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```

maria: Repro note: sequence lengths ~8192, batch=4, serving on a single A100-40GB. Before fused-attn ramp we were stable.

alex: I saw one failing CI shard with similar trace. Two quick observations: the slab allocator growth spikes during rollouts (hot allocation bursts) and the block-table growth correlated with longer decoding sessions.

alex: Quick profiler snapshot (nsys) showed a big gap: attention kernel latency down, but memory pressure up during KV write phases.

jin: This smells like allocation amplification: fused-attn changed kernel tiling and temporarily increased per-head KV writes which blow up number of small page allocations. Slab coalescing not kicking in.

sam: Also worth noting: batching heuristic changed to prioritize latency by increasing micro-batch flushes. That increases churn on KV because we create more short-lived slab objects per request.

luis: Can we confirm page_size vs block_size mismatch? If fused-attn writes larger contiguous KV chunks but pager still uses 128B slots, fragmentation skyrockets. What are current defaults on that node?

maria: On failing node config: page_size=256, slot_size=64, slab_bucket=16MB, eviction_threshold=0.5.

jin: ok that explains it. Bigger writes + small slots -> many partial pages pinned = eviction can't free enough. Two mitigation ideas: 1) increase slot_size to 256 or 512, 2) lower eviction_threshold to 0.25 to trigger earlier compaction.

alex: We tried bumping slot_size to 256 in a quick build and repro still happens but later (about ~30% more throughput before OOM). So helpful but not enough. Eviction tweak seems promising.

perf-bot: [regression] paged-attn:memory-usage increased by 28% on 2026-03-09 after fused-attn merge (p95 memory usage). See perf dashboard /perf/runs/18459.

sam: Another angle — change in kernel changed kernel->runtime copy pattern. Previously we did a single big cudaMemcpyAsync for the KV write, now we do multiple smaller ones per head. That increases CUDA allocator fragmentation because of interleaved temporaries. Need to check whether fused-attn intentionally split the copy.

luis: Running a quick microbench: replacing multiple copies with a single gather+single copy reduces resident_pages by ~12% locally. Will push a debug patch that fuses the memcpy.

maria: Good. Meanwhile can we apply a conservative config change to the fleet to stop customer impact? My vote: lower eviction_threshold to 0.3 and set a temporary hard cap on resident_pages per-worker (max_pages=16000) with forced compaction when exceeded.

jin: If you set forced compaction you'll cause extra latency sometimes. But it's better than OOM. Also enable background defrag to reduce fragmentation. Flag: --kv-background-defrag=true.

alex: Proposed temporary change to rollout: 1) --eviction-threshold=0.3 2) --kv-background-defrag=true 3) --max-resident-pages=16000 4) throttle micro-batch flushes by 10% to reduce churn. Test on canary 10% of fleet.

maria: Sounds good. I'll create a canary with those flags and monitor. Can someone prepare a perf dashboard with resident_pages, eviction_count, avg_evict_latency, and OOM_count?

perf-bot: Dashboard snippet: resident_pages (canary) dropped by 22% after flags applied in local run. eviction_count increased x1.4 but avg_evict_latency stayed <5ms. No OOMs in 30m test.

luis: Pushed memcpy fusion patch to debug/fused-memcpy (non-prod). If that lands, we should be able to revert the temporary slot_size increase. I'll open a PR.

sam: Long-term we should: a) Add a kernel-level hint surface for expected KV write size so pager can pick slab vs page allocation, b) add adaptive slot sizing by workload, c) make eviction policy aware of pinned_slots ratio rather than absolute threshold.

maria: Agree. File follow-ups:
- maria: create canary rollout (in progress)
- luis: PR for fused memcpy (WIP)
- jin: RFC for adaptive slot sizing (please include workload classification)
- alex: dashboard + alert tweaks (set OOM alert sensitivity)

sam: One more datapoint — I ran a long-lived chat workload with seq=12k, batch=2 and the pager did periodic compactions every ~45s, but after fused-attn it never reclaimed the pinned partial pages because pinned_slots stayed high. That's why eviction_threshold didn't help earlier.

maria: Good to know. If background defrag fixes fragmentation, eviction will be effective. Can we also instrument pinned_slots by origin (kernel vs runtime) so we know whether it's kernel pinning or user-level pinned frames?

jin: I'll add a small telemetry event for pinned_slot_origin in the next debug build.

maria: Thanks all — canary is rolling now (10% of dedicated pool). Will report back in ~30m. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Canary started at 2026-03-10T14:12:00Z for config {eviction_threshold:0.3, kv_background_defrag:true, max_resident_pages:16000, microbatch_throttle:10%}. Monitoring channels: #eng-runtime, /perf/runs/18460.

maria: Update 14:39 — preliminary canary: resident_pages -18%, OOM_count=0, tail latency +3-6ms when compaction runs (expected). Keeping canary running for 2h.

alex: Nice. If stable, we should chain a small rollout and merge luis' memcpy patch before rolling further.

maria: Will do. Closing for now, will reopen if OOMs reappear.
